rows.rationale: The seven captured templates keep visitor, exhibition, editorial or policy content available. Membership, tickets and newsletter prompts are identifiable and related to the institution; the parking journey completes without a booking or modal interruption. No autoplay media is recorded. Hidden menu promotions do not establish visible distraction.
rows.nextEvidence: No further evidence is needed for this bounded expectation; recheck after relevant changes.

rows.rationale: Prices/free-for-members and booking labels are visible, and the task stays outside purchases. No cookie banner is observed in these fresh states, while the cookie policy offers Manage Preferences and third-party tracking loads. The preference manager, defaults and accept/reject routes were not exercised; neither fair consent choice nor deceptive behavior is established.
rows.nextEvidence: Open Manage Preferences, inspect defaults and operate accept/reject routes with a visual comparison; do not interpret no observed banner as consent compliance.

rows.rationale: The gallery page explains opening times and free admission, exhibitions identify dates and ticket routes, Stories distinguishes Read/Listen/Watch, and the sustainability statement explains website-specific actions. Parking instructions include the location and advance contact details. These support the bounded English information tasks, without representative-user comprehension or clinical/physical-access claims.
rows.nextEvidence: No further evidence is needed for this bounded expectation; recheck after relevant changes.

rows.rationale: The seven pages retain the same What's on, Visit, Art, Learn, Shop and membership navigation, labeled Search and footer newsletter/privacy pattern. Section headings and contextual links identify the different page purposes. This supports naming consistency, not proof of a maintained design system.
rows.nextEvidence: No further evidence is needed for this bounded expectation; recheck after relevant changes.

rows.rationale: No video or initial animation is recorded. Narrow and reduced-motion states contain eight or nine running one-iteration DIV/SPAN transitions on the shared interface, later absent in live/cold dark states. Effect properties and visibility are not captured, so these cannot establish either harmful motion or proportionate preference handling.
rows.nextEvidence: Inspect the shared transition effects and visible movement while changing reduced motion and using navigation.

rows.rationale: The six information pages and cookie policy record no notification permission calls, with no visible unsolicited alert dialog. Newsletter signup is a deliberate optional action. This is limited to captured states with browser notification permission already denied.
rows.nextEvidence: No further evidence is needed for this bounded expectation; recheck after relevant changes.

rows.rationale: Print emulation removes navigation and retains main text. Tate Modern labels its map as PDF with size and offers white/yellow print and digital communication cards; the exhibition offers a large-print guide. Their contents and print pagination were not inspected. These accessibility alternatives have a clear purpose, so neither optimization nor equivalence/removal is justified from links alone.
rows.nextEvidence: Inspect the map and large-print/communication-card content, their sizes and rendered output before suggesting document changes.

rows.rationale: Shared UI/vendor, page chunks, experimentation and tracking scripts have bounded initial coverage only. Later gallery accordions, listing filters, menus and ticket paths are not comprehensively represented. Unexecuted ranges are investigation targets, not demonstrated dead code.
rows.nextEvidence: Capture representative interaction coverage and identify concrete unused modules with source or deployment corroboration.

rows.rationale: The network already separates runtime, vendors, TateUI and page-specific modules, with additional third-party functionality. The packet does not establish each component's later need and usable activation, so further splitting or removing a component is unresolved.
rows.nextEvidence: Trace one costly optional component from initial request to activation, retaining required gallery information and usable controls.

rows.rationale: Main tasks and headings remain at 360 CSS pixels and most templates avoid overflow. The narrow cookie-policy state does overflow; long tracker/vendor tables are a plausible cause, but their boundaries and controls were not exercised. Narrow navigation and gallery controls were not tested for task completion.
rows.nextEvidence: Inspect the narrow policy table/overflow and operate affected navigation and disclosure controls before classifying a layout defect.

rows.rationale: Stories labels reading, audio and video and the gallery offers digital/print resources; these help format choice. The greener-website page explains a dark, image-light design, but its 70–80% OLED statement is conditioned on maximum brightness and is not a measured saving for this visit. A supported contextual comparison for users' media/print choices is not captured.
rows.nextEvidence: Establish task-value and delivery differences for one meaningful media/document choice before adding impact guidance; avoid labels on every control.

rows.rationale: The homepage Tate Modern card and Accessibility section are activated, and the resulting readable page includes twelve disabled parking spaces via Park Street plus advance phone/email booking instructions. Captured body text and the separate walkthrough support the declared information-completion task; no booking or physical access success is inferred.
rows.nextEvidence: No further evidence is needed for this bounded expectation; recheck after relevant changes.

rows.rationale: Gallery/exhibition/editorial images have strong task value. The sample uses WebP/responsive hero choices and proportionate 279–500 pixel cards, with lazy loading on listings; some homepage cards are eager. Existing dimensions are plausible at common densities, but artwork detail, all renditions and task-image quality were not visually inspected. No removal or smaller rendition is proven safe.
rows.nextEvidence: Inspect representative artwork/hero rendition quality at desktop/narrow pixel densities before any image reduction.

rows.rationale: Tate regular body faces use swap with Arial/Helvetica fallbacks; light/bold variants occur where used, while several declarations remain unloaded. Icon fonts declare block, but body text has a fallback and visible controls have names in the captured sample. This meets the bounded observed typography strategy without assuming all glyph ranges are unnecessary.
rows.nextEvidence: No further evidence is needed for this bounded expectation; recheck after relevant changes.

rows.rationale: All seven documents declare en-GB and a main region with meaningful visible page headings. What's On and Creating a greener website use H2 rather than H1; that alone does not contradict a meaningful primary heading. Search has an ARIA name, footer email a label, filters and accordion controls visible text. This does not establish valid markup, full filter semantics or WCAG compliance.
rows.nextEvidence: No further evidence is needed for this bounded expectation; recheck after relevant changes.

rows.rationale: Each sampled document has a descriptive title and a matching usable absolute canonical. No JSON-LD blocks are declared; missing optional descriptions on several content pages are not by themselves a failure for these tasks. Full structured-data/schema coverage is outside this narrow check.
rows.nextEvidence: No further evidence is needed for this bounded expectation; recheck after relevant changes.

rows.rationale: Task text survives desktop, live preference changes and cold dark/reduced-motion loads. The greener-website page has an intentional dark design in every state; other templates remain light, which alone does not establish a defect. Shared transitions still appear under reduced motion without enough effect information to judge applicability or response.
rows.nextEvidence: Inspect the shared DIV/SPAN transition effects under reduced motion and confirm whether their movement needs suppression.

rows.rationale: Gallery, exhibition, stories and sustainability reading content remains in fresh no-JavaScript states, with expanded gallery information useful for the parking task. However the cookie-policy page loses its 24,027-character vendor/cookie list and Manage Preferences material, leaving about 1,438 characters without an explicit alternative for the declared policy-reading task. Full-sample core content therefore fails.
rows.nextEvidence: Render the cookie inventory and a usable policy/control alternative in HTML or link an equivalent no-script document.

rows.rationale: The record contains experiment/geo-device lookup, analytics/advertising and listing resources, sometimes repeated with differing events. It does not establish which updates are task-required or redundant, nor whether privacy choices altered them. URL repetition cannot justify safe removal or backend-cost claims.
rows.nextEvidence: Inspect initiators, event purpose and consent state for repeated third-party calls before reducing or deferring them.

rows.rationale: Versioned Tate CSS/JS expose long public immutable policies plus validators; external helpers and image responses have lifetimes or validators. Short analytics/experiment policies serve different purposes. This supports the sampled public-asset policy, not measured warm reuse or offline support.
rows.nextEvidence: No further evidence is needed for this bounded expectation; recheck after relevant changes.

rows.rationale: Core Tate scripts/styles use gzip. On What's On, successful consenTag.js (6,565 bytes) and popup_silent.html (12,023 bytes) responses have no content-encoding. These are material third-party text assets, whereas tiny advertising responses are not a basis for failure. Achievable transfer/energy savings are unmeasured.
rows.nextEvidence: Verify and enable beneficial compression for the consent-provider script and document, while keeping consent behavior functional.

rows.rationale: The initial path proceeds through named primary links with a solid blue focus outline. However the first focused Skip navigation link sits at y=-42.24 with height 35.20, entirely above the viewport on all seven pages while scrollY is zero. The generic visible flag does not resolve that geometry: its focus indicator is offscreen. This is a bounded skip-link issue, not a claim of a trap or complete keyboard failure.
rows.nextEvidence: Move the focused skip link into the viewport and confirm it remains visible and activates the main-content target.

rows.rationale: Creating a greener website explicitly identifies tate.org.uk, explains device/server/production impacts and lists mitigation including CMS change, removing video banners/GIFs, improving image delivery, editor guidance and code/data refinements. This meets the disclosure expectation despite the automatic common-path discovery missing it. Execution and estimate verification are separate.
rows.nextEvidence: No further evidence is needed for this bounded expectation; recheck after relevant changes.

rows.rationale: Root and well-known carbon.txt return 404; no usable header/DNS delegation or parseable document is established. This is narrow absence within discovery, not a judgment of the actual Tate website statement or emissions.
rows.nextEvidence: If useful, expose a valid carbon.txt linked to the existing website-specific disclosure and supported relationships.

rows.rationale: The website statement describes server electricity/cooling and digital reductions but does not identify a provider/service and independently corroborated operational hosting scope for this origin. An efficient CMS is not proof of sustainable electricity supply.
rows.nextEvidence: Supply the hosting-service relationship and independently corroborated operational evidence for that boundary.

rows.assessmentScope: Tate Digital Green Team governance for reducing the tate.org.uk website footprint over the reported 2019–2023 baseline/progress period, plus continuing actions described on the public Digital and Creating a greener website pages captured 2026-11-06. Assess accountable review, monitored result and consequent action or reasoned continuation for that web-service commitment. No organization-wide governance or unpublished meeting evidence is in scope.
rows.rationale: Public self-report identifies the Digital Green Team, regular meetings since 2019, estimated 2019/2023 results and completed/continuing actions for this website. That is substantive operational context, but no dated review links a monitored result to a resulting decision or reasoned continuation. The scoped implementation chain remains incomplete without demanding organization-wide minutes.
rows.nextEvidence: Provide one dated Digital Green Team review tying the website result to a chosen next action or reasoned continuation.

rows.assessmentScope: Anonymous English readers using desktop Chromium with pointer input and JavaScript, 1440 by 1000 CSS pixels: start at https://www.tate.org.uk/, follow the Tate Modern gallery card, open Accessibility, and read the accessible-parking location plus advance-booking phone/email instructions. Completion is obtaining public information; no parking booking, ticket purchase, account, contact or form submission. Keyboard-only, assistive-technology, constrained-device and physical-gallery accessibility are outside this assessment scope.
rows.rationale: The exact anonymous desktop pointer route obtains accessible-parking location and advance contact instructions without login, contact or purchase. The full text includes twelve spaces via Park Street and booking phone/email; no material barrier prevents this information task. Keyboard/assistive-technology and physical-gallery access are outside the frozen scope.
rows.nextEvidence: No further evidence is needed for this bounded expectation; recheck after relevant changes.

rows.assessmentScope: The tate.org.uk web service and Tate Digital Green Team commitments described in Creating a greener website: assess the stated 2019 estimated 45 tonnes CO2e baseline, reported 2023 estimated 27 tonnes CO2e result, metric/boundary comparability and ongoing reduction direction as published on 2026-11-06. Exclude Tate buildings, collection transport, commercial shop origin and total organizational emissions; published estimates are self-report, not verified measurement.
rows.rationale: Tate publishes a website-specific reduction direction and estimated 45 tonnes CO2e in 2019 versus 27 tonnes in 2023, attributing improvement partly to the CMS. These are relevant dated metrics for the declared service, unlike corporate-only goals. However traffic boundary, model inputs and methodological comparability are not supplied; a comparable baseline/progress judgment remains unresolved. The numbers are attributed self-report, not independent verification.
rows.nextEvidence: Publish the calculation boundary, traffic/model assumptions and method changes for the 2019 and 2023 estimates so readers can assess comparability.

topFindings.summary: Bring the focused Skip navigation link onto the screen.
topFindings.recommendedAction: Fix the focus-state positioning and verify keyboard activation reaches main content across the shared template.

topFindings.title: Keep the cookie inventory readable without JavaScript.
topFindings.summary: Keep the cookie inventory readable without JavaScript.
topFindings.recommendedAction: Render the list in HTML or link an equivalent static policy; retain a usable preference-management route.

topFindings.title: Compress the material consent-provider script and document.
topFindings.summary: Compress the material consent-provider script and document.
topFindings.recommendedAction: Validate content negotiation with the provider, then confirm consent still works after compression.

topFindings.title: Explain the comparable basis of the reported website footprint reduction.
topFindings.summary: Explain the comparable basis of the reported website footprint reduction.
topFindings.recommendedAction: Add the baseline/result calculation method and boundary, and one dated review-to-action example; retain the existing website-specific disclosure as useful context.
